skill.name: sast-bandit
skill.description: Scan Python projects with Bandit SAST, map findings to CWE and OWASP, and guide remediation for common Python security issues.

security_audit.summary: The static findings are explained by Bandit configuration, pre-commit templates, and Markdown remediation examples. No evidence found of malicious intent, prompt injection, active secret access, or hidden data exfiltration in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: External command examples require user control.
remediation.suggestion: Keep install and scan commands framed as user-approved actions, especially when installing packages or running pre-commit hooks.

remediation.issue: Vulnerable examples may trigger automated scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Continue labeling vulnerable snippets clearly and prefer no-code report output when scans may include sensitive source excerpts.

content.value_statement: Python teams need a repeatable way to find insecure patterns before release. This skill guides Bandit scans, prioritizes results, and maps fixes to CWE and OWASP.
actual_capabilities: Guides Bandit scans for Python files and directories.
Prioritizes findings by Bandit severity and confidence.
Maps Bandit test IDs to CWE and OWASP Top 10 categories.
Provides remediation guidance for SQL injection, command injection, weak cryptography, and deserialization issues.
Includes baseline Bandit and pre-commit configuration templates.
limitations: Only targets Python code that Bandit can parse.
Requires Bandit installation or permission to install it.
May miss business logic flaws and runtime-only vulnerabilities.
Bandit reports can expose code snippets unless no-code output is used.

use_cases.title: Review Python pull requests
use_cases.description: Run Bandit before merge and focus review on high-confidence security findings.

use_cases.title: Add security checks to commits
use_cases.description: Use the pre-commit template to block risky Python changes before they enter the repository.

use_cases.title: Triage legacy code risk
use_cases.description: Create a baseline scan, rank findings, and plan fixes by CWE and OWASP category.

prompt_templates.title: Run a basic scan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner scan for a Python project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan this Python project with Bandit. Summarize high and medium findings with file locations and plain-language risk.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Bandit report. Group findings by priority, explain likely exploit impact, and identify false-positive candidates.

prompt_templates.title: Create a CI gate
prompt_templates.scenario: Add security scanning to pull requests.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Bandit CI gate for this repository. Recommend thresholds, exclusions, and failure rules for pull requests.

prompt_templates.title: Plan remediation by framework
prompt_templates.prompt: Map these Bandit findings to CWE and OWASP categories. Create a remediation plan with owners, priority, and verification steps.

output_examples.input: Scan a Python service before a release.
output: High priority: command execution uses shell input and needs argument lists with validation.
Medium priority: debug configuration should be disabled before production deployment.
Next step: rerun Bandit after fixes and store a no-code report for audit review.

output_examples.input: Triage a Bandit report for a pull request.
output: The strongest finding is a possible SQL injection in the request path.
Two low-confidence findings appear tied to tests and can be reviewed for documented suppression.
The pull request should wait until the SQL issue is fixed or proven unreachable.

output_examples.input: Prepare a security baseline for an old repository.
output_examples.output: The baseline should record current high and medium findings, block new high findings, and schedule remediation by OWASP category.

best_practices: Run scans in read-only or sandboxed environments when reviewing untrusted repositories.
Use no-code report output when findings may include secrets or sensitive source snippets.
Document every suppression with a clear security justification and review owner.
anti_patterns: Do not suppress broad Bandit rules without a reviewed exception process.
Do not treat a clean Bandit scan as proof that the application is secure.
Do not publish reports that include credentials, tokens, or private code snippets.

faq.question: Does this skill run Bandit automatically?
faq.answer: It guides the agent through Bandit workflows. The user should approve package installation and scan commands.

faq.question: Which languages are supported?
faq.answer: The workflow is focused on Python because Bandit analyzes Python source code.

faq.question: Can it replace manual security review?
faq.answer: No. It helps find common static patterns, but reviewers must assess business logic and exploitability.

faq.question: Can findings be mapped to compliance frameworks?
faq.answer: Yes. The included references map Bandit tests to CWE and OWASP Top 10 categories.

faq.question: How should teams handle false positives?
faq.answer: Review low-confidence findings, document justified suppressions, and keep suppression rules narrow.

faq.question: Can this be used in pre-commit hooks?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes a pre-commit configuration template with Bandit and supporting security hooks.
